originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Bohman-Warnke (arXiv:1808.01065, directly fetched) proves existence of one near-complete high-girth regime ((1/6-o(1))n^2 triples, arbitrary fixed girth) with no second regime, no same-vertex-set pairing, and no edit-distance comparison. Prazmowska-Prazmowski weaving (arXiv:1403.4916, directly fetched) introduces the weaving product and proves series of anti-Pasch STS (second regime only) with no pairing, no separation measurement, and no stability claim. The archived pair is not a replay of either: G* is a random-order greedy maximal Pasch-free partial STS, H* is a Bose-priority greedy maximal Pasch-free partial STS honestly labeled as an algebraic/weaving-regime proxy and explicitly NOT claimed to be a certified Prazmowska weave product, so no misattribution. Single-regime existence theorems (including Ling-Colbourn-Grannell-Griggs anti-Pasch constructions) do not mechanically imply two co-located near-complete Fano-free linear families with certified Omega(v0^2) separation on one vertex set; random-permutation counting does not produce the certified distance and provenance. Adjacent cells (DeBiasio-Jiang codegree/rings; Collier et al. linear cycles) state no linear-host density-1 stability separation. Internal prior scan confirms gap: nearest validated finding SCOPE054 is linear 4-uniform Fano expansion density window, a different cell; nearest failure SCOPE-FAIL-20260908-042 concerns exact n=9,10 maxima via link-graph induction, a different claim and route. No source states or implies the exact paired datum (574/621 edges, 1177 separation at v0=63 with replayable verifier).
